rows.why: Drawing carries a printed 85.00 degree callout with leader arrows onto the two collar point tips; the callout convention was independently validated on french-in-8cm (printed 145, drawing measured 151). Drawing shows pointed tips, no tip buttons, one band button; photo matches on family and button configuration. Photo spread off a 50px-gridded render: vertex (405,505), tips (250,690) and (625,665), giving 40 and 54 degree half-angles, total 94 vs drawn 85. The 14 degree asymmetry shows the model is rotated off-axis so this is 94 plus or minus 10. Across all ten leafed photos measured the same way the apparent-spread ranking matched the drawn-callout ranking monotonically. DEFECT: necktie plus fastened throat button completely conceal the collar band.

Button count contradiction. At 16x nearest-neighbour raw-pixel zoom of both collar leaves, button-down-collar-with-78cm-stand.jpg has NO button anywhere on either leaf; its only button is a single throat button on the band, inside the triangular gap where the leaves cross. The convention is verified inside the family: point-in-7cm-with-button.jpg, at identical scale and viewpoint, draws a distinct 4px circle on each leaf just above the tip PLUS the throat button, so this illustrator does draw tip buttons when they exist. The photo shows tip buttons on BOTH points (left ~(320,720), right ~(755,715), each confirmed at 4x) and hides the band and its throat button entirely behind a necktie. The photo adds two buttons the drawing lacks and conceals the one it has. Secondary and weaker: the drawing prints 90.00 degrees and measures ~95 as drawn, while the photo projects 76.9 degrees with a 5.9 degree left/right asymmetry as the error bar. ESCALATE THE DRAWING TOO: a file named button-down-collar that draws no button-down is a source defect. Also note 7.8 cm is not a plausible collar-stand height - real stands run 3-4.5 cm - so that number looks like a point length mis-filed as a stand.

Drawing: 115.00 degree callout, pointed tips, NO tip buttons. Photo shows sharp-pointed tips, clean and bare - correctly distinguished from collar-cutaway-55-btn, its only real sibling (the two illustrations differ by ink-region mean 20.2, attributable to the two tip buttons alone). Measured spread: vertex (400,490), tips (140,655) and (660,640), 57.6 and 60.0, total 118 against drawn 115 - closest agreement of the three 115 degree options. COULD NOT MEASURE: the 5.5 cm point length. This matters because cutaway-55 and large-cutaway-75 carry the SAME 115 degree callout and are separated in the catalog only by point length, which no drawing prints.

Drawing: 115.00 degree callout plus two small circles at the collar point tips (button-down). Photo shows exactly two buttons, one at each collar point tip at (130,600) and (655,605), plus the band button - count and placement match. Spread from vertex (395,495) to tips (110,640) and (680,640): 63.0 degrees each side, perfectly symmetric so the subject is square to camera, total 126 against a drawn 115. Reads 11 degrees wide but is unambiguously in the widest non-french class and comfortably wider than the 100/105 degree photos measured identically (99, 101). Separation from its no-button twin rests entirely on the tip buttons and they are plainly visible and correctly counted. COULD NOT MEASURE: 5.5 cm point length, no printed length callout anywhere in this family.

The one option where the drawing itself was measured rather than the callout trusted. On a common scale the drawn crossover vertex sits at (378,425) with leaf tips at (155,485) and (600,480), giving half-angles 74.9 and 76.1 - a drawn spread of 151 against the printed 145. That validates the callout convention for the whole shirt-collar family. Photo: vertex (300,580), tips (95,700) and (640,700), total 130. The 11 degree left/right asymmetry shows the subject is rotated, and horizontal foreshortening of a collar across a curved chest compresses apparent spread, so 130 for a 145 flat drawing errs in the expected direction and magnitude. Strongest check: measured by one identical method this is the widest of all ten leafed photographs and its drawing is the widest of all ten drawings, by a large margin in both.

Drawing shows a full TURNDOWN collar with two large angular leaves - traced on a 900px render each leaf has a top-inner corner, an outer wing point reaching past the shoulder/yoke lines, an upward notch apex and a centre-front point, six exterior vertices across the pair. The photo shows an upright band/stand collar with NO leaves at all. Quantified against the neck-opening width at the collar top edge, validated first as comparable (290px drawing vs 270px photo on a common render): the drawn collar lowest point sits 1.62 neck-widths below its top edge, the photographed collar 0.80 - roughly half as deep. Vertical foreshortening on a near-frontal chest accounts for 1.0-1.2x, nowhere near 2x. The photo matches the option LABEL and description but the drawing is the authority.

Drawing: 115.00 degree callout, pointed tips, no tip buttons; photo matches family and button configuration. Measured spread: vertex (355,468), tips (85,660) and (700,690), half-angles 54.6 and 57.2, total 112 against drawn 115. Sits in the correct band relative to same-method measurements of the 100/105 degree photos (99, 101) below and french (130) above. COULD NOT MEASURE: the 7.5 cm point length, the sole catalog discriminator between this and collar-cutaway-55 since both are drawn at 115 degrees. Here the band button, the only plausible shared scale landmark, is hidden behind the tie knot. Raw pixel lengths across photos at different framings are meaningless and were not used.

Drawing: 105.00 degree callout, pointed tips, no tip buttons; photo matches family. Measured spread: vertex (395,480), tips (195,660) and (605,640), half-angles 48.0 and 52.7, total 101 against drawn 105. First visual impression from the contact sheet was that this looked too narrow for a large cut-away; measuring corrected that impression, which is why the measurement is reported rather than the impression. COULD NOT MEASURE: the 8.0 cm point length, the only thing separating this from its 115 degree siblings. Normalising point length by neck width across photos was attempted and discarded - each photo uses a different model at different framing and the resulting ratios inverted the label order, so the landmark did not validate.

The drawing cannot settle this. large-round-in-53cm.jpg and round-in-53cm.jpg are different files but effectively the same drawing: resampled to a common 300x300 and differenced over the ink region only, mean absolute difference is 16.9/255 - LOWER than the 20.2 measured between cut-away-in-55cm and its with-button twin, whose only genuine difference is two 4px tip buttons. Both carry identical 100.00 degree callouts and both labels say 5.3 cm. Confirmed: the photo shows a club collar with fully rounded tips, no points, band button visible - correct family. Cannot confirm which of the two round options it is. Angle reading discarded: a club collar has no sharp front-edge crossing so the vertex is ill-defined. This is a catalog spec defect, not an image defect - no regeneration can fix it.

Drawing: 90.00 degree callout, pointed tips, NO tip buttons - which is what separates it from collar-mid-cutaway-70-btn, whose drawing is identical apart from two small circles at the tips. Photo shows pointed tips with no tip buttons, correct. Measured spread: vertex (395,597), tips (295,690) and (500,685), about 96 against a drawn 90. Least confident reading in the batch: the tips sit low in frame against a dark suit so tip localisation is soft by about 25px, i.e. 10 degrees. Note this option and collar-af1-70 are drawn only 5 degrees apart, below photographic resolution, so that pair is not distinguishable regardless of image.

Drawing: 90.00 degree callout plus two small circles at the collar point tips. Photo shows exactly two white buttons, one anchoring each collar point tip, plus the band button; count and placement match. Spread from vertex (400,395) to tips (100,700) and (700,690): 44.5 and 45.5 degree half-angles, total 90 - the closest agreement with a drawn callout in the batch, and the near-perfect symmetry means the model is square to camera so no rotation correction is needed. NOTE: the catalog description says a throat button, which the drawing contradicts - the drawing shows tip buttons. The drawing wins and the photograph follows it, so the description is what needs fixing.

The drawing filed for this row shows a plain band/stand collar with one throat button, NO tab and NO collar leaves - the same artwork as rolled-stand-collar.jpg at 1.64/255 mean absolute difference. The photo agrees with that drawing: band collar, single silver stud at the band base, no leaves, no tab. So photo and drawing match, but they match on something that is not a one-piece 7.5 cm collar with tab. A tab is a large unmistakable feature - a fabric strap crossing behind the knot - and it is absent from BOTH. Because the drawing is the authority and has no tab, the photo cannot be called WRONG; but the drawing is almost certainly mis-filed, since its own length-siblings one-piece-collar-in-85cm-with-tab.jpg and -9cm-with-tab.jpg are visibly different artwork with a different viewpoint, vertical CF placket and offset button.

This drawing is the outlier of its family: oblique skewed projection, NO printed angle callout where its three siblings all print 60.00 degrees, and the left collar leaf drawn turned up. At 22x nearest-neighbour zoom a ~5px ring is drawn at the LEFT collar point only; no button is drawn at the right point. The photo shows a long point collar with a white 4-hole button and buttonhole at the LEFT point and a completely BARE right point, verified at 4x on crop x640-880/y600-780. Projected spread, apex at the leaf crossing (555,350) to tips (318,715) and (770,700), is 33.0 + 31.6 = 64.6 degrees with only 1.4 degrees left/right asymmetry. Two readings remain and the drawing cannot settle them: either the photo faithfully copies a drawing that itself exposes one button, or the intended option is a two-tip button-down like all three callout-bearing siblings and the photo is missing the right button. DEFECT either way: the left/right button asymmetry is not a real garment, and the band is hidden by a necktie.

The photo matches its drawing on every feature: band/stand collar, no leaves, one white 4-hole button at the band base, softly rolled top edge, band fully visible with no necktie. What blocks a pass is sibling separation, not photo quality. rolled-stand-collar.jpg is effectively the SAME artwork as one-piece-collar-in-75cm-with-tab.jpg - mean absolute pixel difference 1.64/255 at native size, only 1.6% of pixels differing by more than 40, and those differences are 1px shifts on the CF seam and inner band edge visible in a red/cyan overlay - and near-identical to one-piece-collar-in-8cm-with-tab.jpg at 2.93/255. Three catalog options share one drawing. COULD NOT MEASURE: band height - no length callout on any of the three drawings, and scaling from the photo would require assuming a real-world garment size.

Same root cause as collar-large-round-53: the two source drawings are pixel-equivalent over the ink region (mean diff 16.9/255), carry identical 100 degree callouts, and both labels state 5.3 cm, so the illustration cannot adjudicate which photo belongs to which option. Confirmed on this one: club collar with fully rounded tips and no points, band button visible. Its spread does measure cleanly - vertex (400,465), rounded tip bottoms (185,630) and (590,645), giving 52.5 and 46.5 degree half-angles, total 99 against the drawn 100. So the image is consistent with its own drawing; it simply is not separable from its sibling.

Drawing shows a band-only mandarin stand collar: no leaves, band front ends cut square, a narrow vertical gap between the band ends at centre front, a small step where the band meets the shirt front. No angle callout, correctly, since spread is undefined for a band collar. Photo matches on every structural point including the square-cut ends that separate it from the rounded-stand sibling in the same techpack folder. Critically this is one of only two images in the batch photographed with NO necktie and the throat open, so the band - the entire discriminating feature - is fully visible. NOTE: the catalog description contradicts the drawing, describing collar points cut with a squared-off end, i.e. a squared POINT collar. The drawing shows no points at all; the description needs fixing.

The drawing's printed callout reads 0.6cm, contradicting the row's 0.1 cm label, and the drawing wins. This is also the only drawing in the family rendered at 221x221 rather than 192x192, so its offsets are not directly comparable to siblings without rescaling. The photo does show a tonal stitch line inset from the leaf edge and turning the point, so the stitching is present on the correct part. But neither discriminator resolves: offset in cm is unmeasurable (no scale landmark in the photo, and the drawings do not encode offset to scale), and the AMF-versus-machine distinction is not readable - at 6x on a 160px crop this stitch's pitch, length and regularity are indistinguishable from the machine siblings, with none of the long widely spaced slightly irregular pick stitches that make AMF identifiable, as they obviously are in stitch-03-amf.

Two blockers, both in the source data. First, machine-01cm-top-stitching.jpg is BYTE-IDENTICAL to machine-03cm-top-stitching.jpg (md5 8e910bc6bbdd1d964c7e92557800de00, 8241 bytes each), so 0.1 cm and 0.3 cm cannot be told apart. Second, the drawing's printed callout reads 0.3cm, contradicting the row label, and the drawing wins. Tested whether the drawn offset encodes the printed number by measuring the red stitch line offset from the collar edge on the right leaf across the family, all normalised to 192x192: printed 0.1cm gives 4px, 0.3cm gives 4px, 0.5cm gives 5px, 0.6cm gives 4px. The drawn offsets do NOT scale with the printed values, so those two measurements disagree and neither is validated - unlike the collar-angle callouts, these stitching drawings do not encode their dimension to scale. The photo does show the right feature class: a fine tonal machine topstitch parallel to and inset from the leaf edge.

The drawing's printed callout reads 0.1cm, contradicting the row's 0.3 cm label, and the drawing wins. The photo is the only one in the batch showing a genuine AMF signature - long, widely spaced, slightly irregular pick stitches following the leaf edge and mitring round the point - so the construction class reads correctly and is distinguishable from the machine group. Two problems stop it passing. The offset is unverifiable for the same reason as the rest of the family. And the stitches are rendered in RED contrast thread while all seven siblings are tonal white-on-white; red is the drafting convention every one of these drawings uses to highlight the stitch line, so the photo appears to have literalised an annotation colour as real thread. Since thread colour is a separate option group in this catalog, a customer would read this photo as a thread-colour choice rather than a stitch-offset choice.

Same drawing file as stitch-01-top, byte-identical at md5 8e910bc6bbdd1d964c7e92557800de00, so the two options cannot be separated by their illustrations. Here the printed callout 0.3cm does agree with the row label. The photo shows a fine continuous tonal machine topstitch inset from the outer edge of both leaves and turning both points - correct feature class and garment part. But the discriminating dimension is the offset and it is unmeasurable: the drawing does not encode offset to scale (4px for 0.1cm, 4px for 0.3cm, 5px for 0.5cm, 4px for 0.6cm at 192x192) and the photograph carries no scale landmark.

This is the only drawing in the family carrying NO callout at all and no detail-bubble inset - it just draws a dense red zigzag along the leaf edge, so there is no printed dimension to hold the photo to. Whether that zigzag is meant to sit ON the edge at offset zero or is merely a bolder rendering of the same nominal line cannot be decided: by eye it rides the edge, but the same automated offset scan that returns 5px for the printed-0.5cm top-stitch drawing also returns 5px here, so the two readings disagree and neither is validated. The photo shows a tonal stitch line clearly INSET from the leaf edge with ordinary machine pitch and no readable AMF signature, so it neither confirms the drawing's edge-riding zigzag nor its AMF class, and there is no quantitative content in the drawing to check it against.

machine-05cm-top-stitching.jpg is BYTE-IDENTICAL to machine-06cm-top-stitching.jpg (md5 7a75c65c1f4fb2cbbea798f622252ab5, 8227 bytes each), so 0.5 and 0.6 cm share one drawing. The printed callout reads 0.5cm, agreeing with this row. The photo shows a tonal machine topstitch inset from the leaf edge - right feature class and part - and by eye its inset looks the widest of the four top-stitch photos, but that will not be converted to cm: the drawing does not encode offset to scale, and the photos are framed at different zooms with no shared landmark, so cross-photo pixel offsets are not comparable.

Same drawing file as stitch-05-top (md5 7a75c65c1f4fb2cbbea798f622252ab5), and its printed callout reads 0.5cm, contradicting this row's 0.6 cm label with the drawing winning. So the drawing both contradicts the label and is shared with a sibling. The photo shows a tonal stitch line parallel to and inset from the leaf edge and turning the point - right feature class. DISCARDED READING recorded: the stitch character initially read as a discrete hand/pick stitch rather than a machine line, but on a matched 6x zoom against 01-top, 03-top, 05-top, 01-amf and 05-amf every one resolves into discrete stitches at that magnification, so beaded-versus-continuous is not a valid discriminator at this resolution.

The illustration this row points at is a 300x300 grey placeholder card bearing the literal word None rather than a technical drawing, but the parallel techpack file images/techpacks/shirt/decoration_stitching_on_collar/none.jpg draws the intent properly: a collar whose leaf edge is plain and unstitched in the detail bubble. The photo shows a point collar whose leaf edges are completely clean, no stitch line on either leaf, checked at 2x on the left-leaf crop (80,150)-(480,550) and on the full frame. Unambiguously separable from all seven siblings, every one of which draws a stitch line along the leaf edge. Absence is the entire spec and absence is what the photo shows.

Drawing 0110 marks a bare chest slit on the wearer left chest: red stroke 225px long = 23.5% of the drawn shoulder span, raked ~10 degrees upward toward the outside, drawn as a slit with NO flap. The photo shows a flapped pocket at a HIP position. Measured: mouth is a dark slit running x 95 to 880+, essentially level at 1.3 degrees rather than the drawn 10; below it hangs a flap with hem at y 870-890, depth 245px, confirmed by vertical gradient scans at two columns. A besom has no flap at all. Position also contradicts: a full-length vertical dart runs (455,0) to (470,590) and terminates exactly at the pocket mouth - the signature of a hip pocket - and no lapel, gorge, collar or shoulder appears anywhere in frame to support a chest location. File is byte-identical (sha256 0afb0647) to cp-trapezoid, cp-welt-23, cp-welt-25 and cp-welt-27.

The notch is outside the frame. Drawing 0006 is a notch lapel whose discriminating feature is a near-closed fish-mouth slit: the collar lower edge runs almost horizontally from (327,318) to (400,327) with the lapel upper edge only ~12px below, a slit ~70px long by ~12px gap, i.e. 0.64 and 0.11 of the drawn 110px lapel width. The photo does establish a two-piece collar-and-lapel construction with its own pick-stitched edge, so not a shawl, and the lapel front point at (275,800) subtends ~30 degrees. But the lapel outer edge runs off the top-right corner at (860,50) with no discontinuity and the model neck skin is visible at the top edge, confirming the crop stops at or above the gorge. The only candidate slit in frame measures 40-60px over 620+px, i.e. 2.2-2.4 lapel widths, so it is the front-opening shadow rather than the drawn 0.64-lapel-width fish mouth.

The frame cannot settle it. What was measured: the dominant pick-stitched outer edge traces continuously from (830,0) to (130,1060) via a Sobel map on gamma-lifted luminance, with no step, no notch cut-out and no upward peak along its ~1050px visible length, and the two front edges converge to a downward wedge apex at (105,855) with a ~29 degree interior angle - both consistent with a shawl. What could NOT be settled: the frame is cut off above the gorge and below the break, so the shawl defining continuous collar-to-lapel wrap is never in view, and a fine pressed seam from (778,180) to (896,152) meets the outer edge without interrupting it - not a notch or peak, but unresolvable between a two-piece shawl joining seam and a gorge. Decisive for grading regardless: this file is byte-identical (sha256 c24c7c80) to lapel-shawl, lapel-shawl-0005, lapel-shawl-0e, lapel-shawl-d and lapel-shawl-asymmetric - one photo serving all six shawl rows, so it cannot be right for Asymmetric Shawl Collar and Shawl 0A simultaneously.

Drawing 064Q is a macro of a hand-worked keyhole in bright cyan: squared bar-tack at the LEFT, pierced round eye at the RIGHT, straight. Photo shows exactly that in bright cyan on a navy notch lapel. Masked-thread principal-axis profile in 20 bins: photo L/W 7.75 vs drawing 6.44; both straight (sagitta/L +0.007 and +0.006); width profile in both peaks in the end-quarter nearest the eye and is flat elsewhere, giving eye/bar 1.52 photo vs 1.44 drawing - 5.5% agreement on the discriminating ratio. Eye right and squared bar left in both, pierced hole visible at (515,578). Distinguishable from lbh-017 (round head), whose ratio is 1.73 photo vs 1.60 drawing - each photo tracks its own drawing.

Drawing 035C, knot but no seal, is a RED macro: squared knot at one end, a rounded UNSEALED unpierced end at the other, straight. Red-dominant mask with principal-axis profiling: photo L/W 6.18 vs drawing 6.40, a 3.4% match. Both straight (sagitta/L -0.006 and -0.004). Correcting for the drawing axis pointing left, the width profiles agree in direction: both narrowest at the squared end and widest at the far end (1.36 photo, 1.63 drawing). Critically the far end in the photo is a rounded swelling with NO pierced eyelet, unlike lbh-005 and lbh-017 which both show an open hole - which is what no seal calls for.

Drawing 00EC, round head, is a purple macro: squared bar-tack left, large open ROUND head right, straight. MEASUREMENT TRAP CAUGHT MID-FLIGHT: an automated mask first gave eye/bar 2.6 by latching onto lapel shading around the eye; re-measuring the outer stitch envelope by hand off a 4x grid gave bar height 37px and eye 64px, i.e. 1.73 against the drawing 208/130 = 1.60, an 8% agreement. The automated number would have produced a spurious rejection. Length/bar 6.4 vs 7.25. Both dead straight. Eye right and squared bar left in both, purple thread in both. Note the two source drawings are themselves only 0.16 apart on that ratio, so the pair is inherently close at the source.

Drawing 055F, arc upwards, is a RED macro bowing convex-upward, squared left, curling to a rounded hook right. Red mask plus principal-axis profiling in 20 bins: centreline sagitta/L +0.150 photo vs +0.151 drawing - the curvature signature matches to three significant figures, and it is OPPOSITE IN SIGN to its sibling lbh-milanese-curved at -0.131, so the two arc options are genuinely discriminable. L/W 8.88 vs 7.29 (18% apart). Correcting for the drawing reversed axis, both widen toward the same hooked right end (1.70 photo, 1.66 drawing).

Drawing 055U is a keyhole worked in three sequential thread colours with red circled numerals 1, 2, 3 over each segment, eye right. The photo reproduces it segment for segment. Sampling mean RGB per column along the thread at 5% intervals: drawing goes light cyan-blue to 0.35, steps at ~0.375 to a deeper blue through 0.65, steps at ~0.675 to violet-grey; photo goes light blue to 0.35, steps at ~0.375 to deep blue through 0.65, steps at ~0.675 to violet. Both transitions land at the same fractional positions, segment proportions ~37.5/30/32.5 in both. Open round eye right, unsealed left, in both. DEFECT worth flagging separately: the photo has BAKED THE TECH-PACK RED CIRCLED 1-2-3 ANNOTATION INTO THE SHIPPED PRODUCT IMAGE - accurate as a depiction of the drawing, but it is manufacturing markup living inside a customer-facing photograph.

Drawing 06EG, arc slight downwards, is an ORANGE macro sagging concave-upward, squared left, curling to a rounded hook right. Orange mask plus principal-axis profiling: centreline sagitta/L -0.131 photo vs -0.131 drawing, exact agreement on the discriminating curvature and correctly opposite in sign to lbh-lumi at +0.150. L/W 8.31 vs 7.55 (10%). Accounting for the drawing reversed axis, both are widest at the hooked right end (1.48 photo, 1.55 drawing) and squared at the left. Thread orange in both.

Drawing 00ED is a lilac macro: uniform-width bar, squared end at the left, plain rounded end at the right, NO enlarged eye, dead straight. Masked-thread principal-axis profiling gives photo L/W 5.77 against drawing 5.63 - a 2.5% agreement, the tightest of the set. Both straight (sagitta/L +0.003 photo, +0.006 drawing). Width profiles near-uniform in both with only a slight swell toward the right: max/min 1.31 photo vs 1.26 drawing, i.e. no keyhole eye in either, which is precisely what separates this from lbh-005 (eye/bar 1.52) and lbh-017 (1.73). File hash unique.

Drawing 00EF carries a red magnified callout inside an ellipse; at 4.5x it resolves as a teardrop with a narrow POINT at the upper-left widening progressively to a broad ROUND HEAD at the lower-right, length 168px, head/mid-bar ratio ~1.9, and no squared sealing bar-tack at the tail. The photo, resolved with CLAHE at 5x on tone-on-tone navy, shows the same object: narrow rounded tail at (428,676) widening to a round head centred ~(525,755) with an open hole, outer head diameter ~45px against mid-bar ~24px = 1.9, matching the drawing, total length ~152px, and no squared bar-tack at the tail. Orientation matches (tail up-left, head down-right). The absent seal and the progressive taper are what separate it from lbh-005, lbh-017 and lbh-pinpoint, all of which show a crisp squared bar.

Drawing 02J1 red-outlines an applied patch on both hip fronts: a closed quadrilateral, top edge only 6.8 degrees off level, height/width 585/295 = 1.98, square top corners, softly rounded bottom corners, NO flap. The photo shows a flap pocket instead. Measured: flap top fold from (745,245) to (78,595) = 27.7 degrees BELOW horizontal, raked not level; flap depth 205px left end, 255px right; mouth length ~750px so depth/length 0.27-0.34, the inverse proportion of the drawn 1.98:1. Profiled for a patch body before judging: over rows 830-1210 the column-mean absolute gradient never exceeds 1.94 (a broad soft drape fold spread over ~30 columns) against 4.45 in the flap-edge band, and there is no localized vertical gradient where a patch side seam would descend. No patch bag, no bottom edge, no side seams below the flap - it is a slanted flap pocket, a different option. File is byte-identical (sha256 4660e3dc) to 12 other options including cp-patch, lp-patch-flap, lp-patch-rounded and all three lp-patch-btn-tab variants.

Drawing 3411 marks three things: a round BUTTON on the waistband, a small buttonhole slot at the waistband end, and critically NO extension tab, the waistband terminating flush at the fly. Siblings differ on exactly these: 3410 replaces the round button with a filled hook bar and has no button, 3412/3413/342A add a large protruding tab respectively pointed, rounded and square, 3416 shows TWO buttons. The photo shows a single four-hole button, an adjacent horizontal buttonhole slot, no protruding extension tab of any shape beyond the fly line, and no hook bar. Button count 1, tab absent, hook absent - each attribute individually excludes a different sibling, so this is a three-way independent confirmation. Minor rendering defect not affecting identity: button and buttonhole sit side by side rather than the button passing through the hole.

Drawing knot-d shows a HORIZONTAL pocket whose end callout carries a straight vertical stitched bar with a semicircular arc bulging outward from it - the flat side plus the bow of a D. At 5x the photo shows precisely this at the left end of a horizontal welt pocket: a dense vertical bartack bar spanning the pocket end with a clean semicircular arc sweeping outward into the panel, closing the D. Both the pocket orientation (horizontal, matching the drawing rather than the vertical pockets of knot-i and knot-dash) and the compound bar-plus-arc shape match. Separable from knot-hip-i, which shares the horizontal pocket but has a plain vertical I bar with no arc. Thread is tonal.

Drawing knot-dash shows a VERTICAL pocket whose end callout carries only a SHORT dash, clearly shorter than the mouth width and offset to one side, in deliberate contrast to knot-i whose bar spans the full mouth. At 6x with brightness enhancement the photo shows a compact densely-stitched short bar tack at the lower end of a vertical pocket opening, projecting to one side of the slit rather than bridging it. Orientation and the short one-sided form both match, and it is visibly a different construction from the knot-i photo. Medium rather than high because the pocket is rendered as a very narrow closed slit rather than an open mouth with two measurable edges, so the tack length could not be expressed as a fraction of mouth width - the comparison is qualitative.

Drawing knot-hip-i shows a HORIZONTAL hip pocket - the callout draws both welt lips as horizontal lines - with a vertical I bar at the pocket end spanning the full height across both lips. At 5x the photo shows exactly that: a horizontal double-welt jetted hip pocket with a dense vertical bartack at its left end running the full depth of the opening and crossing both welt lips. Pocket type (horizontal jetted hip, not the vertical front pocket used by knot-i and knot-dash), bar orientation and extent all match. Separable from knot-d, which shares the horizontal pocket but adds the semicircular arc absent here.

knot-i shows a VERTICAL pocket with a straight bar of stitching running the FULL WIDTH across the mouth at its end, edge to edge. At 5x the photo shows exactly that: a bar tack spanning edge to edge between the two sides of a vertical pocket opening at its lower end, straight, no curved arc. That separates it from knot-dash (short tack well under mouth width, offset to one side), knot-d (bar plus semicircular arc on a horizontal pocket) and knot-hip-i (vertical bar on a horizontal jetted hip pocket). DEFECT not reconciled: the tack is rendered in bright RED thread, whereas red in this drawing set is the highlight convention marking the graded feature - the same red marks the seam in 3130, the welt in 3132 and the stripe in 3121. The generator appears to have literalised the highlight as thread colour. Not failed on it because the graded attribute is tack GEOMETRY, which is correct.

Matches the No Topstitch sibling, not this option. The field discriminators are presence, offset and count of a stitch line along the front pocket mouth: 31A1 (0.15cm) puts the red line hard against the pocket seam with no gap, 31A3 (0.6cm) shows a clear band of fabric between seam and stitch, 31A6 has no red at all, 31A9 shows two parallel lines. At 5x with brightness 2.0 and contrast 1.6 - a setting at which the individual twill wales of the cloth are clearly resolved - there is NO stitching visible anywhere in the frame, not along the pocket mouth and not along the fly J. Every seam renders as a bare pressed fold. Absence is treated as evidence rather than a resolution limit because the sibling photo pocket-stitch-pick-015, at the same 0.15cm scale and same render size, resolves individual stitches easily.

Drawing 3302 highlights a stitch line hugging the front pocket mouth with no visible gap - the 0.15 cm condition. At 5x with brightness enhancement the opening carries a clear line of DISCRETE, EVENLY SPACED RAISED STITCHES sitting directly on the folded edge, unmistakably a hand pick stitch rather than a continuous machine line, with no band of fabric between edge and stitch. That excludes pocket-stitch-none, both 0.6 cm siblings (31A3 shows a visibly separated line) and pocket-stitch-double (two parallel lines; only one here). SOURCE PROBLEM worth recording: 31A1 (0.15 cm topstitch) and 3302 (0.15 cm pick stitch) are graphically near-identical - neither dashes nor otherwise encodes topstitch versus pick stitch - so the drawing alone cannot separate this option from pocket-stitch-015. The photograph settles it here.

No pocket opening is depicted at all. Drawing 3104 belongs to a 6-member shared template registered to a common frame (waistband depth 104px, belt-loop pitch 445.5px). Sibling 3130 red highlight sits exactly on the full-height vertical line, proving that line is the SIDE SEAM; the graded feature is a stitched slant mouth running from the waistband down to terminate ON the side seam with a bartack. The photo shows only one crisp stitched full-height seam on the silhouette and one SOFT PRESSED FOLD that starts at the waistband and fades out around y=1000 with no bartack, no corner and no stitched mouth edge - confirmed at 4x on the convergence region. Taking the fold as the mouth anyway gives a corrected offset of 1.28 waistband-depths against the drawn 0.62, roughly double and landing between the 3.2 and 5.1 siblings, with a vertical run of 6.4wb against the drawn 2.6wb. Failure is at the coarse level - no depicted mouth - not the fine cm level. No centimetre figure is recoverable; the drawings carry no printed callout.

Drawing 3121 red-highlights the pocket mouth itself, i.e. contrast piping along the opening, on the same geometry as plain sibling 3101 (top corners agree, 424 vs 427 in the registered frame - a cross-check on the calibration). The photo shows a slant front pocket whose mouth carries distinct NAVY CONTRAST PIPING its full length, from the waistband seam at (405,272) to a bartack corner at (280,706) near the side seam. Mouth Dy 3.84wb against the drawn 3.95wb for 3.2 cm, a 3% match and closer than 5.1 cm at 4.16wb. Reservation stated plainly: the corrected Dx reads 1.29wb against a drawn 0.89wb, about 45% over. The offset excludes the 2.0 and 2.5 stripe siblings by more than 2x but does NOT cleanly separate 3.2 from 5.1; the mouth-length ratio is the tiebreaker and favours 3.2.

Matches drawing 3102 element for element: front pleat hanging from the waistband, slant mouth as a crisp double line from (285,245) descending to a clean V bartack at (410,575) ON the side seam, side seam continuing full height below it, and beyond it a back dart over a horizontal double-jetted BACK pocket - the back-pocket furniture present in every drawing of this family. Landmarks: waistband depth 106px (106/105 at two columns), belt-loop pitch 327.5px. Mouth Dx 1.18wb, Dy 3.11wb. Horizontal foreshortening factor from belt-loop-pitch/waistband (photo 3.09 vs drawing 4.28) = 0.72, giving a corrected offset of 1.63wb against the drawn 1.77wb for 5.1 cm (-8%) and against 0.89wb for 3.2 cm (+83%), comfortably excluding every narrower sibling. Unresolved: the mouth vertical run is 3.11wb against a drawn 4.16wb, and the side seam is not visible above the bartack.

Drawing 3178 red-highlights a small horizontal pocket immediately below the waistband seam on the viewer left, drawn as a filled slit (besom) rather than an outlined raised strip. The graded feature is absent and a different garment part is foregrounded. The drawing's whole differentiator is a standing collar band, drawn as a closed rectangle across the back neck. Sampling the centre column x=600 returns TWO separate ink runs - y44-51 (band top edge) and y111 onward (band lower edge, where the centre-front line begins) - a 59px band gap; at 4x the two horizontals are joined by side edges and the band rises above the shoulder points. The photo shows no band whatsoever: the charcoal waistcoat's collar terminates at the shoulder and the white shirt collar sits free all the way around the neck, identical to the notch-lapel-vest photo. NOT a crop problem - the neck and shirt collar are fully in frame at exactly the height a band would occupy. The photo depicts the sibling notch-without-collar-band option.

Drawing shows a notch lapel and, at the back neck, a single neckline curve: sampling the centre column x=600 returns one continuous ink run from y=75 downward, i.e. no collar band, where the band siblings return two runs at the same column. Blueprint shows lapels whose points project upward and outward past the gorge plus a distinct rectangular collar band across the neck. Drawing shows peak lapels with tips angled up toward the shoulders; centre column x=600 returns one continuous ink run from y=69, so no collar band. Clearly distinct from the notch and shawl siblings. COULD NOT MEASURE: no printed dimension callout, so no cm lapel-width or peak-angle claim is made - deliberately not assumed from the label.

Same test as its notch counterpart. The drawing has a collar band: centre column x=600 returns two ink runs (y70-78 and y109 onward), a 30px band gap, confirmed at 4x as a closed band with side edges rising above the shoulder points, whereas shawl-lapel-vest returns one continuous run from y68 at the same column. Drawing shows one continuous unbroken shawl curve with no notch and no peak; centre column x=600 returns one continuous ink run from y=68, so no collar band. Distinguishable from notch and peak siblings by the unbroken edge and from shawl-collar-stand by the absent band.

Counted the red-marked buttonhole positions with saturated-red blob detection: drawing 5 (y-centres 512/617/723/830/935 on a 1200px canvas), photo 5 (y-centres 456/580/707/839/974 on 1168px). Drawing is an interior cutaway with two interlining zones: a dense chest fill ending at a boundary above the welt pocket, then a distinct dash-row fill continuing past the pocket to the hem. Photo matches that topology - coarse brown haircloth over the chest terminating at a curved seam, then cream linen canvas, hand pad-stitched, continuing past and below the welt pocket to the frame edge, visibly floating (peeled clear of the shell), sewn, with raw canvas edges. Normalised to the welt pocket, the only landmark present in both images, the chest-material boundary sits 0.32 pocket-heights above the pocket top in the drawing and 0.40 in the photo, both measured from cropped views rather than assumed. Two sewn interlining layers running the whole front is exactly full canvas. COULD NOT MEASURE: the Chinese hatch-legend callouts are illegible at source resolution so the fills cannot be decoded by name; and the photo crops above the hem, so full-length coverage is inferred from uninterrupted continuation rather than seen reaching the hem.

The drawing places a clear material boundary ABOVE the welt pocket: coarse brick/grid fill over the chest, then a visibly different diagonal-lattice fill from roughly 0.29 pocket-heights above the pocket top downward, and that lower fill carries its own leader line and callout, so the two-material split is deliberate rather than a drafting artefact. The photo shows no such boundary anywhere: identical diamond hand pad-stitched linen canvas runs continuously from the shoulder, around the welt pocket, and on to the bottom of frame with no change of material, plus a coarse haircloth panel at the armhole. Canvas that never terminates is full-canvas construction; the photo is not distinguishable from what vest-canvas-full claims and it contradicts the termination the drawing draws. Verified by matched same-coordinate crops of all three canvas drawings and a 2x crop of the photo pocket zone. Medium not high because the drawing's Chinese hatch-legend callouts are illegible at source resolution, so the lower material cannot be named - the verdict rests only on presence versus absence of the boundary, which is directly observable in both.

Blueprint is an interior cutaway with a shaped chest piece over a base interlining and a taped front edge; the live photo shows dense rows of hand pad-stitching over at least two distinct tan interlining layers, which is the signature of hand-canvassed construction and the opposite of a single fused layer. It is also not separable from the shipped Full Canvas and Fused Canvas photos, which show the same pad-stitched cutaway language.

Same base cutaway as its two siblings with only the fills changed. Ink density measured over one identical column (x640-860, confirmed by overlay to sit on the interlining zone rather than the outline or facing band) puts uncon lowest through the chest - 0.11-0.25 across y300-620 against half at 0.34-0.45 and full at 0.40-0.53 - and below the pocket it carries the sparsest stipple of the three. The drawing therefore gives this option the least interlining of the set. The photo instead shows a teardrop chest piece covered in dense diamond HAND PAD-STITCHING sewn onto a full-length floating linen canvas with hand pick-stitching and raw edges - the same hand-canvassed construction its full-canvas sibling shows. Pad-stitching is the signature of canvassing and contradicts Unconstructed Chest on its face; this is the same defect that already failed vest-canvas-single. Ruled out the obvious misread: the cream is garment canvas, not the linen dress form - it has pad-stitch texture, hand stitching along the armhole and raw frayed edges, while the dress form behind it is smooth and unstitched.

Blueprint is a plain vest front with no chest pocket drawn. Drawing: 2 saturated-red blobs, centroids (838,447) and (823,483), stacked 36px apart, both right of centre = wearer's left lapel. Saturated-red blob detection returns 0 marks on the drawing and 0 on the photo; the same detector returns exactly 1 and exactly 2 on the two sibling pairs in this batch, so it is validated rather than merely null. Blueprint shows the vest interior with a red piping line along the junction of the front facing and the lining; the live photo shows the garment open on a hanger with bright red corded piping running that exact facing/lining seam from shoulder to hem, and a zoom on the mid-body confirms a finished sleeveless armhole, so it is a vest interior and not a jacket.

Correct arc vocabulary - squared start at the waistband, smooth sweep, clear terminal downward hook, which is what separates 3135 from its three siblings - but the far end is on the wrong side. NOTE: the direction premise conflicts with the suit-2pc grading and is recorded as CONTESTED.

Best match in the batch. 3136 profiles as a drop from the waistband, a clearly ROUNDED corner with visible radius unlike the sharp 90 degrees of 3133, then a near-flat run to the side seam ending with no hook. The photo reproduces all three. Quantitatively the closest of the whole batch: run travel 225px / belt-loop pitch 330px = 0.68 against the drawing 305/445 = 0.69, within 2%. Drop depth 50px against waistband depth 90px = 0.55 versus the drawing 0.96 - right order of magnitude, unlike jeans-square at 2.7. Unambiguously distinguishable from square by corner radius, from diamond by absence of a point, from arc by absence of a terminal hook.

All three discriminating features match 3133. Confirmed front view via fly J-topstitch with waistband closure above. Mouth is an L: vertical drop at x=362 from the waistband seam to y=593, a corner, then a straight run to the side, ending flat with no downward hook. Corner radius is crisp, effectively 90 degrees with no easing, which is precisely what separates 3133 from round (visible radius), diamond (downward point at the far end) and arc (long drop plus terminal hook). Run length 272px/315px = 0.86 versus drawing 0.69, inside foreshortening tolerance. DEVIATION not reconciled: the vertical drop is ~3x deeper than drawn (photo 301px against waistband depth 112px = 2.7, drawing 0.83). Vertical-to-vertical, so foreshortening does not excuse it. Not treated as disqualifying because drop depth is not what separates this option from its three siblings - all four drawings have a drop, and the corner and end treatment are correct.

Right feature, right seam, right place. Illustration 165588 marks the option as a thin line running ALONG the front pocket mouths on both sides, so the stitch belongs on the front pocket opening, not a back pocket or hem. The photo shows a stitch line parallel to and inboard of the front pocket mouth. Character is correct for PICK rather than machine topstitch: at 6.5x the line resolves into discrete regularly spaced stitch points with visible gaps, not a continuous chainstitch, which separates it from pocket-stitch-06 and pocket-stitch-double. NOT MEASURABLE: the 0.6 cm cannot be verified - the drawing carries no dimension callout and draws the stitch directly on the mouth line, encoding zero offset. Reported as a ratio instead: 34-43px from the mouth edge, roughly 0.10-0.12 of front-panel belt-loop pitch, generous for a 0.6 cm pick stitch but with no drawing-side number to compare against.

Correct direction and correct plain edge, wrong magnitude. Normalising horizontal mouth travel by belt-loop pitch - a ratio of two horizontal spans on the same curved surface, so hip foreshortening largely cancels - gives photo 133px/330px = 0.403 against drawing 3120 at 79px/445px = 0.178. That is 2.3x the drawn 2.0 slant, and the residual bias runs the wrong way for rescue: the mouth sits in the outer third where compression is worst while the loop pitch spans the flatter middle, so 0.403 UNDERSTATES the true ratio. Angle agrees: 15.3 degrees from vertical against 8.9 measured on the drawing. At 0.403 the photo lands between the 3.2 sibling (~0.285) and the 5.1 sibling (0.445), nearest 5.1 - not distinguishable as the narrowest slant in the family. The label ratio is self-validating: drawing travels 79px and 198px, ratio 2.51, against labels 5.1/2.0 = 2.55.

Correct feature and direction, wrong magnitude. The cream contrast piping is present along the pocket mouth, which is exactly what 3120 adds over 3100. Both checks are independent and agree, and foreshortening cannot explain it since the travel/pitch ratio is taken between two horizontal spans on the same curved hip.

Width is right, mouth runs backwards. Navy piping isolated by colour: top (247,250) to bottom (402,668). DIRECTION IS: an equalized crop shows the folded centre-front edge at x~690 with the fly J-topstitch to its right, so going DOWN this mouth x increases toward the fly, ending near the pressed crease rather than running out to the side seam. Mirror- and viewpoint-invariant, so not explicable as the opposite leg. NOTE: this direction claim conflicts with the suit-2pc grading of the same feature family and is recorded as CONTESTED - see DEFECT-FAMILIES.md.

Both-sidedness is right; the feature is not a watch pocket. The only watch-pocket photo in the batch that actually shows a watch pocket. 3186 draws a flap hanging from the waistband seam on the front panel, deeper than its welt/besom siblings (69px vs 46 and 48) with a downward point in the centre of its lower edge. DEVIATION: width 0.48 of belt-loop pitch versus 0.285 drawn, about 1.7x wide, and since foreshortening compresses horizontal spans the true width is larger still - a genuine overshoot. Not disqualifying because a pointed diamond flap with a button is unmistakable against its siblings at any width. NOT VERIFIABLE: the label says Right and no fly or closure appears in frame, so handedness could not be established.

Same failure as watch-right-welt: this is the BACK besom.
